description:
Fail-closing at the NormalizedCost layer does not reach consumers that read the raw cost float, so a fallback-priced number still lands in the local database, in plots, and in platform rankings. Both external reviewers independently found comparison.py; agy additionally found the per-query path.

Verified ungated consumers:
- benchbox/core/results/database.py:361-364 - writes total_cost into the SQLite results table
- benchbox/core/results/database.py:477 - persists per-query execution.cost
- benchbox/core/visualization/result_plotter.py:256,271
- benchbox/core/analysis/comparison.py:693-696 - ranks platforms by price/performance and computes potential savings from unverified numbers
- benchbox/core/cost/tco.py:341 - base_annual_cost = total_cost * annual_runs
- benchbox/core/results/normalizer.py:203

Upstream of all of them, integration.py:109-110 stamps query_result["cost"] per query regardless of resolution quality.

Also in scope, R14: optimizer.py has 20+ pricing call sites driving savings recommendations. Any recommendation built on a fallback price must be suppressed with a stated reason, not computed. Today an unknown node type makes current_price and us_east_price both $1.00, so the branch at optimizer.py:700-708 returns None and the recommendation vanishes silently - the right outcome reached by accident, for the wrong reason, and only in that one branch.

The principle: a cost that is not fit to publish is not fit to rank, plot, persist, or advise on.
